items.title: Meshy Wants AI for 3D Creation to Feel More Like a Creative Partner
items.excerpt: Meshy has opened its conversational 3D Agent to all users -- a multi-step AI built specifically for 3D creation that keeps context across a chat so game artists can brainstorm, batch-generate related asset families, and convert concepts into textured, riggable models inside one workflow, positioning generative 3D as a creative collaborator rather than a one-shot prompt.

items.title: The Relic: First Guardian director confirms AI use after YouTubers sound the alarm over a preview build
items.excerpt: After creators flagged suspected AI content in a preview build of Soulslike The Relic: First Guardian, the director says AI touched only the early concept stage -- a few loading-screen concept pieces and consumable icons -- with none in the final game. A window into how studios are actually folding generative AI into the concept/design pipeline and the disclosure norms that now shape it.

items.title: Steam Week in Review: more than half of new Steam games could carry an AI disclosure by 2027-2028
items.excerpt: Steam AI-disclosure rates have climbed from 10.9% of releases in 2024 to 30.8% so far in 2026; on trend, over half of new Steam games could be AI-flagged by 2027-2028 -- a concrete measure of how fast generative AI is being folded into game production. Weaker craft hook (an adoption stat), included as funnel context.

items.title: Nexus Mods finally tightens the screws on AI — though it's still playing softball with the tide of slop
items.excerpt: The largest PC game modding platform is toughening its policy on generative AI, now requiring modders to properly disclose AI-generated assets in their uploads — a workflow/craft shift for the modding community as the platform grapples with AI 'slop'.
